_what: Two Meta ad-format pages, reduced to the structure the image row's anchor has to discriminate between.
_readThisBeforeTrustingIt: THESE ARE NOT CAPTURED PAGES. They were written by hand to carry the structural
difference the anchor rests on: both pages publish an identical Text
Recommendations block and the SAME 'Primary Text' label, and they differ on the
File Type line — JPG or PNG on image, MP4/MOV/GIF on video.
WHAT A TEST ON THIS FIXTURE PROVES: that anchorDiscriminates() reports the right
verdict when given a page pair shaped this way — that it rejects an anchor
present on both, and accepts one present only on the image page.
WHAT IT DOES NOT PROVE: that Meta's real video page lacks the new anchor. Only a
live fetch settles that, which is why scripts/migrateFixMetaImageAnchor.js
fetches BOTH pages on every run and refuses to write if the new anchor turns up
on the video page. A fixture cannot stand in for that check and must not be read
If somebody later captures the real pages, replace these strings and delete
_synthetic — but keep the migration's live check either way. A fixture ages; the
